H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: H-OS-L1 (Pebble) n=95 mean=7.15 std=1.78 confidence=strong. Best sample size in dataset with 66% positive. Strong site traffic signal (26/95). Qualitative data shows 10-minute settle, excellent music reception (10 Liked/9 Loved). AutoGluon zone prediction 6.859 underestimates observed 7.15 (delta +0.29) — model may be conservative on overstim protocols. YouTube reach low (30 views).
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: Pebble is the most tested overstimulation protocol and shows strong, consistent calming effects. Listeners report grounding and reduced sensory overload, with high music appreciation.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall

AutoGluon prediction matches observed.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Rainfall matches Pebble's efficacy closely. Listeners also settle around ten minutes and find the music calming, though more neutral opinions appear.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier

H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Glacier has the tightest score spread among overstimulation protocols. Listeners describe a spacious, calming feel with a five-minute settle time and balanced music reception.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow

sphere_commentary.overview:
The dataset reveals consistent positive efficacy across all three series with HEALING leading in sample size and consistency, while TRANSFORMING shows greater variance as expected for ascending-arc protocols.
• HEALING protocols dominate sample volume (n=574) with stable means near 7.0 and strong confidence tiers
• THRIVING shows slightly higher mean scores but tighter variance, suggesting stable efficacy for HOLD-type designs
• TRANSFORMING carries the widest spread (std=1.87) consistent with ascending-arc work in low-affect states
• YouTube reach and retention data uniformly unavailable (2-3 day lag) limiting engagement analysis
• Cross-run embedding drift below 0.85 for all protocols indicates analytical framing instability or genuine pattern evolution
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The three series display distinct efficacy profiles that reflect their design intent.
• HEALING: most consistent listener response with lowest variance and highest per-protocol sample sizes
• THRIVING: highest mean scores in Focus & Clarity (Summit 7.63) but variability across Maintenance & Balance
• TRANSFORMING: broadest outcome distribution, especially in Mind & Clarity (Cosmos 5.7) and Motivation & Drive (Footpath/Trail ~6.3)
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several structural and analytical anomalies warrant investigation.
• X-MC-L3 (Cosmos) n=10 mean=5.70 std=2.45 — possible population mismatch or early-drop signal in Mind & Clarity
• All 30 protocols show cross-run embedding similarity <0.85 — suggests analytical instability or evolving protocol effects
• AutoGluon cross-bucket routing repeatedly selects X-ME (Mood & Energy) protocols for zones outside their design category
• Crisis protocols (H-CR-L1/L2/L3) cluster at structural floor (~6.4) with AutoGluon predicting 1.5+ points higher
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Five concrete protocol development actions emerge from convergent analyzer signals.
• H-CR-L1/L2/L3 (Anchor/Harbor/Horizon) n=43/33/27 mean~6.4-6.5 — investigate whether adviser routing matches acute listeners appropriately
• X-MD-L1/L2 (Footpath/Trail) n=22/14 means 6.36/6.21 — ascending-arc motivation protocols underperforming; consider extending hold phase or adjusting entrainment curve
• T-FC-L3 (Summit) n=35 mean=7.63 — highest THRIVING score; investigate groove style differentiation for pattern replication
• X-MC-L3 (Cosmos) n=10 mean=5.70 std=2.45 — investigate population split by analysing contextual responses or adjust routing criteria
• H-OS-L1 (Pebble) n=95 strong performer with site traffic (26/95 from site src); scale traffic to this protocol while retention data matures
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift analysis shows substantial analytical instability across the protocol library.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: All 30 protocols show similarity <0.85 (range 0.507-0.821) indicating either genuine pattern evolution or model framing inconsistency
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Too few protocols with embeddings for cluster analysis — cannot identify analytical isolation patterns
• Confidence note: Drift this extensive suggests either protocol effects are evolving with population changes or Sphere’s analytical framing needs stabilization

by_protocol.X-ME-L2: X-ME-L2 (Sunrise) n=25 mean=6.76 std=1.71 confidence=meaningful. Comparable efficacy to Breeze. Qualitative data shows variable settle time, strong music reception (7 Loved/6 Liked). Cross-bucket routing also flagged by AutoGluon. Minimal YouTube data.
by_protocol.X-ME-L3: X-ME-L3 (Updraft) n=18 mean=6.28 std=1.74 confidence=developing. Lower mean (6.28) and limited data merit further scrutiny. Qualitative data shows 5-minute settle, balanced music/rhythm reception. No YouTube presence.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Listeners using Meadow for anxiety and stress report a noticeable calming effect, usually settling in within ten minutes. The music is widely liked, and the protocol shows strong, consistent results.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Cottage provides a similar calming experience to Meadow, with listeners settling a bit faster (around five minutes). Opinions on the music are more mixed, but the overall effect is positive.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Valley also helps with anxiety, with a slightly longer settle time of about ten minutes. Listeners find the rhythm very settling, and outcomes are in line with the other anxiety protocols.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Anchor is used in acute distress and shows a modest but meaningful improvement. Listeners settle quickly (within five minutes) and report significant improvement, though the music reception is varied.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Harbor performs similarly to Anchor, with a slight edge in positive reports. Some listeners find the music neutral, which may affect the experience for those in crisis.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Horizon shows the quickest settle time in the crisis set, but a notable minority dislike the music. This suggests the groove style might not suit all listeners in acute states.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Pebble is the most tested overstimulation protocol and shows strong, consistent calming effects. Listeners report grounding and reduced sensory overload, with high music appreciation.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Rainfall matches Pebble's efficacy closely. Listeners also settle around ten minutes and find the music calming, though more neutral opinions appear.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Glacier has the tightest score spread among overstimulation protocols. Listeners describe a spacious, calming feel with a five-minute settle time and balanced music reception.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Lantern is a strong sleep aid, with most listeners settling within five minutes and loving the music. It shows the highest positive rate in the sleep set.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Hammock has the most consistent scores for sleep. Listeners take about ten minutes to settle, and music opinions are more neutral, but the calming effect remains solid.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Midnight performs on par with the other sleep protocols. However, a higher number of listeners find the rhythm slightly busy, which may not be ideal for sleep onset.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Ember helps creative flow for about half of listeners, but some need more time to settle. The music is well received, making it a pleasant backdrop for creative work.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Current improves on Ember with a tighter score range. Listeners settle in ten minutes and strongly enjoy the music, suggesting a smoother creative experience.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Aurora shows the highest creative flow scores, but with fewer listeners. Those who tried it report a ten-minute settle and balanced rhythm, hinting at a more targeted groove style.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Compass helps focus for just over half of listeners, but some find the rhythm slightly busy. It may need a longer hold phase to better support concentration.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Waypoint is a clear step up for focus, with two-thirds reporting improvement. Listeners settle in ten minutes and find the rhythm balanced, making it a stronger focus tool.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Summit is the top performer for focus, with 71% positive change. Some listeners note a strong but slightly unsettling effect, suggesting the groove is powerful but intense.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Stone supports emotional maintenance well, with a tight score range. Unusually, many listeners take 20 minutes to settle, and therapy sessions are a common context.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Axis has a wider score spread for maintenance. Listeners settle in five minutes, but rhythm opinions are split between balanced and busy, indicating possible groove variability.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Orbit shows a high positive rate but with very few listeners. Concerningly, some did not settle at all, which conflicts with its maintenance purpose.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Cavern provides modest clarity improvement. Listeners take about ten minutes to settle and largely love the music, making it a calming choice for mind clarity work.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Starlight mirrors Cavern with similar scores and strong music reception. The small sample limits confidence, but the pattern is consistent.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Cosmos scores notably lower with high variability, suggesting it may not suit the typical listener for mind clarity. Rhythm opinions are mixed, with some finding it too busy.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Footpath offers a gradual motivation lift rather than an immediate boost. Listeners report noticeable improvement over time, and the music is generally liked.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Trail follows a similar gradual profile to Footpath. Limited data, but listeners settle in five minutes and mostly love the music.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Switchback shows a higher average motivation score but with wide variability and few listeners. Music reception is positive, but caution is needed due to low sample size.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Breeze has a restorative effect on mood and energy, with just over half reporting improvement. Interestingly, the AutoGluon model suggests it may work well for several other zones beyond its design.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Sunrise performs similarly to Breeze, with strong music reception and variable settle times. It also appears in cross-zone routing, hinting at broad applicability.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Updraft has a lower average mood/energy score with limited data. Listeners settle quickly and find the music and rhythm balanced, but more responses are needed to gauge true efficacy.
